$comment: Broiler.RegEx's rules of the shared JavaScript libraries programme's SL shape (governance section 3.2 of the
programme in Broiler.VM/docs/javascript-shared-libraries/), adopted under the owner condition R10 of milestone SJL-11
(docs/roadmap.md section 6, docs/conventions.md) and ported from Broiler.Unicode's tests/Unicode.Architecture.Tests,
in Broiler.VM's register shape: each row states the rule as it holds this repository's projects - the library
Broiler.Regex, the Native AOT probe probes/Regex.Probe and the two test projects - names the test that asserts it and
the witness it is shown refusing, and has a status. Beside the rules, contractChecks holds the three contract
conventions of the programme's architecture.md section 4 that Broiler.VM's JSD-0081 (section X3) finds Broiler.Regex
breaching and that metadata can decide. Every rule and check is Active, and the library does not yet meet every one:
starting-violations.tsv beside this file is the exact list of what they find in it, which each test asserts in both
directions and SJL-11.2 shrinks to none (bundle sjl-11-001's check E-3). RuleRegisterTests holds this file to the
tests, the witnesses on disk and the list's citations. No row carries a run figure; the list carries the findings.

rules.statement: No library references an engine project or package, anything in Broiler.VM, or any project or package outside the allow-list, and a library references the programme's libraries only in the layering's direction: Broiler.Regex may reference Broiler.Unicode.Algorithms alone, the Unicode owner's provider (requirement R11, decision D11 of Broiler.VM's JSD-0081), and never Broiler.Unicode.Tables, which is test-only data, nor another project of this repository. Every library has a row in the layering table, so a new library cannot pass by being unknown.
rules.evidence: The library's project file (ProjectReference, resolved to the referenced project's assembly name, and PackageReference), its restore (obj/project.assets.json, every package resolved directly or transitively, the SDK's own ILLink package aside) and its built assembly's AssemblyRef table
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The library is read in all three places and names packages that its restore resolves and its assembly references; the witnesses reference an engine project, a Broiler.VM package, a package outside the allow-list, the owner's tables and the probe, each reported; and the assembly half is shown refusing this test assembly, which references xunit and the library.

rules.statement: No library declares a mutable static field, a static array or a static field of a mutable collection type, a settable static property, a [ThreadStatic] field, or names AsyncLocal or ThreadLocal: Broiler.VM's rule N12 (convention 7). This repository adds one kind: a static readonly field holding an object of a class the library declares whose instances can change after construction - an instance field that is not readonly, or one of a mutable collection or array type, in the class or a base class the library declares - which is how a shared set that normalises itself in place on a read is static mutable state (conventions 7 and 10, decision D31). Compiler-generated types and fields are the compiler's, and are left out.
rules.evidence: The Field, Property and CustomAttribute tables, the TypeRef table, and every class's instance fields and base type, of the library's built assembly
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The library declares a constant, which the rule reads as a static field and passes as a literal, and a static field holding an object with no state, which it reads and passes; the witness declares one member of each refused kind, and two objects that change on a read, directly and through a base class, each reported, beside an immutable one that passes.

rules.statement: No library reaches anything on Broiler.VM's B5, B5b and B5c lists (dynamic loading, reflection invocation, Reflection.Emit, LambdaExpression.Compile, native-library and function-pointer marshalling, method preparation, platform invoke, module initializers), generic instantiation over a run-time Type, the Type-taking Enum readers, dynamic, reflection-based serialization, file, network or process I/O, or an environment read (convention 8). The Native AOT probe, an executable that writes its report to a file, is held to every clause except I/O.
rules.evidence: The MemberRef, TypeRef, AssemblyRef, CustomAttribute and ImplMap tables of the library's built assembly and of the probe's, built under the JIT beside this test
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The library's tables are read, and the probe names System.IO.File and is read with I/O allowed; the witness reaches each refused kind once and every one is reported, and read as the probe it still fails on everything but I/O.

rules.statement: No library uses a platform globalization or regular-expression API (convention 9): System.Text.RegularExpressions, any System.Globalization type but NumberFormatInfo.InvariantInfo and NumberStyles, TimeZoneInfo, the clock, string normalization, platform casing, char and Rune classification beyond ASCII, a string comparison that defaults to the current culture, or a number parsed, formatted, converted or interpolated without a format provider. Every Unicode answer is the provider's (decision D11), so the platform's is never one here.
rules.evidence: The TypeRef and MemberRef tables of the library's built assembly, member references read with their parameter types so that an ordinal overload is told from a culture-sensitive one
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The library compares strings ordinally and tests surrogates, and the rule reads those references with their parameter types and passes them; the witness uses each refused kind once, char.IsDigit and char.ToLowerInvariant among them, and every one is reported. ONE STATED LIMIT: a parameterless ToString() on a number is not refused, because every record's generated ToString reaches it; it is a review obligation of convention 6.

rules.statement: IsAotCompatible and IsTrimmable hold for the library, with the trim, AOT and single-file analyzers on, and it targets net10.0 with nullable enabled, implicit usings disabled, deterministic builds, no unsafe code and warnings as errors; nothing is suppressed in it: no NoWarn beyond the SDK's own 1701 and 1702, no WarningsNotAsErrors, no SuppressTrimAnalysisWarnings, no UnconditionalSuppressMessage. An inventory in the shape of Broiler.VM's N36, docs/suppressions.md, lists by file every suppression in the sources and project files of the library and the probe and in the build files they import, and says None when there is none. The Native AOT probe is evaluated with Broiler.VM's root settings (PublishAot, full trimming, InvariantGlobalization, UseSystemResourceKeys, TrimmerSingleWarn off, IsAotCompatible, warnings as errors) and is held to the same absence of suppressions (convention 12).
rules.evidence: The library's and the probe's properties as MSBuild evaluates them, the built library's and probe's CustomAttribute tables, and the text of every source and project file of the library and the probe and of Directory.Build.props, Directory.Packages.props and eng/Broiler.Packaging.props
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The library and the probe are evaluated with every import applied, so a property set in Directory.Build.props or the packaging file and undone in a project file is seen; the inventory scan reads both project files, the sources and the build files; the witness project sets every analyzer on and suppresses one warning, and is refused for that alone, and a NoWarn of the SDK's codes alone is shown to be a reset while one code more is a suppression.

rules.statement: The public API of the library matches its committed baseline, Broiler.Regex/PublicAPI.txt, in both directions: nothing public exists that the baseline does not record, and the baseline records nothing that does not exist. Package validation is enabled for the packed library and reads the last version published to nuget.org as its baseline, 0.1.0-preview.4 until a later one is published (convention 16; bundle sjl-11-001's check E-4). The baseline is rewritten only by a test run with BROILER_REGEX_UPDATE_API=1, and the diff is reviewed like any other change.
rules.evidence: The public types and members of the library's built assembly, read from metadata, against its PublicAPI.txt; the library's evaluated IsPackable, EnablePackageValidation and PackageValidationBaselineVersion
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The library's listing is not empty and it is packed; the witness has drifted from its baseline once in each direction and both are reported, and nothing else is; a packed project without package validation, or validated against another version, is refused.

rules.statement: Generated data is byte-identical to what its generator writes from pinned, hashed inputs. This repository pins no data: decision D11 puts every table the library reads in the Unicode owner's provider, and the library declares no data version of its own. So a source in the library that a generator wrote, which nothing here can regenerate from a pin, is a violation, and so is a data generator script in the library. Generated data a later change adds comes with its pin and a regeneration test in this rule.
rules.evidence: Every file of the library's directory outside build output: a source is generated when its name ends in .g.cs or its first lines carry the <auto-generated> marker; a script is a .py, .ps1, .sh, .mjs or .js file
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The rule reads every file of the library's directory, its project file and its sources among them; the witness, a source carrying the marker under an ordinary name, and a script are each reported, and a hand-written source that names the marker below its head is not.

rules.statement: Every relevant unit of the library carries a Broiler Code Assurance annotation and the generated artefacts are current (decision SJL-D-5 (a)). The configuration, assurance.config.json at the root, covers Broiler.Regex/Broiler.Regex.csproj under the strict exemption predicate with preprocessor directives forbidden; an exclusion gives its reason and hides no source of the library; the artefacts CODE-ASSURANCE.md, HUMAN_REVIEW.units.md and assurance.manifest.json exist and the manifest lists every source of the library; and CI runs the assurance tool's check with --root Broiler.RegEx and fails on drift.
rules.evidence: assurance.config.json against the library; the manifest's files array against every source of the library; .github/workflows/ci.yml; and the assurance tool's check, which that workflow runs
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The library must be covered and every one of its sources must be in the manifest; the witness configuration leaves the library out, uses the narrower predicate, permits directives and excludes a source of the library without a reason, and each is reported, while a configuration that covers the library strictly and excludes nothing is accepted, and a source the manifest does not list is refused. The unit-level half is the tool's own check.

rules.statement: Determinism: two runs, and two concurrent threads, over the probe's population give identical output - every case compiled once, as an engine compiles a pattern once, and matched through the same instances in all four runs, every answer rendered into a report compared as text (conventions 6 and 10). The vectors at library level replace the population when SJL-11.2 adds them (bundle sjl-11-001's part D).
rules.evidence: Four runs, two sequential and two on concurrent threads, of probes/Regex.Probe/ProbePopulation.cs through one set of compiled instances
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Each run answers every case, matches, refusals and the Unicode property escapes among them; the witness answers from a counter and two runs through it differ.

rules.statement: No C# source of this repository's projects (the library, the probe and the two test projects) holds a preprocessor directive, no file of the repository holds a CR, and .gitattributes gives every text file LF line endings (convention 17).
rules.evidence: Every .cs file of the projects parsed with Roslyn, its directive trivia read; the bytes of every file of the repository outside version control's directory, build output, test results, packed artefacts, the witnesses and the package icon; .gitattributes
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Every source of every project is parsed, the generated table and the probe included, and every file read, the adversarial corpus, the workflows and the documents among them; the witnesses hold a conditional region and a pragma, each directive reported by line, and a file stored with CRLF, which .gitattributes keeps as-is.

contractChecks.statement: No public signature of the library names a collection type of the base class library, a delegate that runs the caller's code (Func, Action, Predicate, Comparison, Converter, Delegate), object or Type. The members a class or record gets from System.Object or the compiler's record machinery (Equals(object), EqualityContract, PrintMembers) are not the library's choice and are left out. JSD-0081's section X3 names the collections and the Func types in Broiler.Regex at c1422f4d.
contractChecks.evidence: The public API listing of the library's built assembly, the one rule SL6 compares with its baseline
contractChecks.nonVacuousWhen: The listing holds neutral signatures, which the check reads and passes; the witness names a collection, a Func and object in public signatures, each reported, beside a neutral member and a record, which pass.

contractChecks.statement: No public type of the library derives from an exception. An expected failure is a status (decision D9), and a library throws only on a broken precondition, which a base class library exception states; a public exception type of the library's own is how it reports a failure its contract admits, as JSD-0081's section X3 finds. ONE STATED LIMIT: an exception that a base class library call throws for an input the contract admits (the escaped group names of Broiler.VM's correspondence row S2) is invisible in metadata; bundle sjl-11-001's check A-11 decides it.
contractChecks.evidence: The type lines of the public API listing of the library's built assembly, with their base types
contractChecks.nonVacuousWhen: The listing holds every public type with its base; the witness declares a public exception type for a malformed pattern, which is reported, beside a precondition stated by ArgumentOutOfRangeException, which is not.

contractChecks.convention: 5, limits are explicit and never the stack
contractChecks.statement: No library asks how much stack is left: RuntimeHelpers.EnsureSufficientExecutionStack, RuntimeHelpers.TryEnsureSufficientExecutionStack or Thread.MaxStackSize. How deep the stack lets code recurse differs between the JIT and Native AOT, so a library that probes it has made the stack its limit, as JSD-0081's section X3 finds of the matcher's stack guard. ONE STATED LIMIT: recursion itself is not read here; bundle sjl-11-001's check A-4 decides it over the matcher's IL call graph.
contractChecks.evidence: The MemberRef table of the library's built assembly
contractChecks.nonVacuousWhen: The library's member references are read; the witness calls both stack probes and each is reported.
